questions.q: In the context of static characteristics of a sensor, which of the following signifies resolution?
options: It provides the smallest change in the input that a sensor is capable of Sensing
It is the difference between the standard value and the value produced by Sensor
It is the deviation of sensor value curve from a particular straight line
It represents the correctness of the output compared to a superior system
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): 'resolution is about the smallest change in the input that a sensor is capable of sensing'.

questions.q: What is the general operating voltage range of commercial sensors which are available for circuit enthusiasts and hobbyists?
questions.explanation: Not stated in the lecture transcript; hobbyist sensor modules (DHT, MQ, HC-SR04, PIR) typically run at 3.3-5 V, matching all answer keys.

questions.q: Which of the following actuators produce linear displacement?
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): electric linear, fluid power linear and manual linear actuators all produce linear displacement.

questions.q: IEEE 802.15.4 uses __ protocol for data transmission.
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): for 802.15.4 'The MAC protocol that is typically used is the CSMA-CA protocol'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an operating frequency of ZigBee?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): ZigBee 'operates in three frequencies 868 MHz, 902 to 928 MHz and 2.4 GHz' - 950 KHz is not one.

questions.q: What is/are the role(s) of adaptation layer in 6LoWPAN?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): 6LoWPAN adaptation layer does fragmentation/reassembly, 'compression of header, routing of data link layer'.

questions.q: Maximum payload allowed in wireless HART is ______ bytes?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): WirelessHART 'payload size that is allowed is 127 bytes'.

questions.q: Radio dead-spots can be bypassed using a process called _______.
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): radio dead-spots 'can be bypassed using a process in Z-wave which is known as healing'.

questions.q: In which application domain does ISA 100.11a is primarily used?
options: System for Smart Security and Surveillance
Automation in large scale complex industries
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): ISA 100.11a applications are 'automation in large scale complex industries'.

questions.q: Which wireless communication technology is based on Ad-hoc Piconets?
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): Bluetooth forms 'Ad-hoc networks' organised as Piconets.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation, NFC, stands for?
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): NFC is near field communication (close proximity <10 cm).

questions.q: Which of the following work groups extend the integration of the IoT devices from network to service level.
questions.explanation: Lecture 04 (IoT Networking Part I): 'CoRE ... extends the integration of IoT devices from networks to the service level'.

questions.q: QoS policies for IoT Network includes ______.
questions.explanation: Lecture 04 (IoT Networking Part I): 'QoS policies for IoT networks includes resource utilization, data timeliness, data availability, and data delivery'.

questions.q: Which IoT networking protocol supports caching capabilities to improve the response time and reduce bandwidth consumption?
questions.explanation: Lecture does not discuss caching; among the options only CoAP (RFC 7252) has built-in response caching/proxying to cut latency and bandwidth.

questions.q: Which IoT networking protocol is used in the Military?
questions.explanation: Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): DDS RTPS 'application such as military, industrial and healthcare monitoring'.

sets.source: https://progiez.com/nptel-introduction-to-industry-4-assignment-2-answers

questions.q: Which industrial revolution is coined as “The second Machine Age” by Prof. Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee of MIT?
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): 'the fourth industrial revolution, this term was coined as the second machine age by Prof. Erik ... and Andrew McAfee'.

questions.q: Automation in manufacturing system, computers, the Internet, and usage of renewable energies are some of the advancement in technologies, which took place during the ______.
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): third revolution (1960s) brought computers, digitization, internet; renewables listed alongside.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are probable tipping points in 2025?
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): tipping points by 2025 include 'clothing ... connected to the internet'.

questions.q: Which of the following is provided in a sustainable Industry?
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): 'A sustainable industry basically provides energy efficiency, conservation of resources, and low waste production'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of Information and Communication Technology (ICT)?
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): ICT enables ERP, wireless communication, GPS and RFID systems.

questions.q: How many different categories of countries are there based on population growth?
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): 'three different types of countries based on the population growth'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an optimistic view of population growth?
options: Consumes most of the economic investments in safety, need for schools, hospitals, universities
Increases globalization issue such as trade and commerce
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): 'optimistic view ... increases the globalization issues such as trade and commerce'.

questions.q: Which company developed Lean Production System?
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): lean originated in Toyota (Toyota Production System).

questions.q: Why should companies implement lean approach?
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): lean is adopted 'to reduce the cost, to reduce the time of production, and to improve the quality'.

questions.q: Which of the following cannot be considered as a medium of getting smart and connected?
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): mediums for smart & connected are sensors/actuators, IoT network, cloud, embedded systems - not the manufacturing system.

questions.q: What are the four key attributes of smart business models?
options: Value addition, revenue enhancements, and technologies
Value proposition, revenue centralization, and technologies
Value addition, revenue streams, and emerging trends
Value proposition, revenue streams, and technologies
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): 'key attributes of the smart business model: value proposition ... revenue stream ... technologies'.

questions.q: Which of the following statements are correct?
options: Physical layer is responsible for collecting and acquiring data from object or environment.
Physical layer is equipped with micro-controllers and sensors.
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): physical layer collects/acquires data with sensors and microcontrollers; digital layer stores, analyzes, processes.

questions.q: ______ is a flexible system that can self-optimize performance across a broader network, self-adapt to and learn from new conditions in real or near-real time, and autonomously run entire production processes.
questions.explanation: Lecture 10 (Smart Factories): 'The smart factory is a flexible system that can self optimize ... and autonomously run the production processes'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a component of smart factory?
questions.explanation: Lecture 10 (Smart Factories): components are smart machines, smart engineering, smart devices, smart manufacturing process, innovation, IT, data analytics - not 'smart ideas'.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the use(s) of Big Data analytics in smart factories?
questions.explanation: Lecture 10 (Smart Factories): big data analytics helps 'improving the value streams ... predicting the future ... KPIs'.

questions.q: Which of the following is true regarding Cyber-Physical Systems?
options: They are devices having information processing systems embedded into them.
They are typically confined to a single device
They are networked set of embedded systems
questions.explanation: L11 CPS: embedded system is 'confined to this particular single device' while 'in a cyber physical system ... a network set of such kind of embedded systems'.

questions.q: What are the 5 Cs in the CPS “5C architecture” for Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: L11 CPS: '5C architecture ... Connectivity, conversion, cyber, cognition, and configuration'.

questions.q: What are Smart Sensors?
options: They are the integration of sensors and actuators with a processor and a communication module.
They are universal sensors which can sense a wide range of different stimuli.
They are the kind of sensors which do not require a power source to operate.
questions.explanation: L11 CPS: smart sensors are 'integration of sensors and actuators, with a processor and a communication module'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of Collaboration platform
questions.explanation: L12 Collaboration Platform & PLM: 'pro-work flow ... is the name of a collaboration platform that is often used in the industries'.

questions.q: State true or false — “PLM handles a product completely, from single part of the product to entire portfolio of that product”.
questions.explanation: L12: 'PLM handles a product completely from single part of the product to the entire portfolio of that product'.

questions.q: In PLM, how many phases does a product lifecycle have?
questions.explanation: L12: 'there are five different parts, five different phases in this product lifecycle'.

questions.q: ________ is direct/indirect views of physical world environments which are “augmented” with computer-generated superimposed images
questions.explanation: L13 AR/VR: AR = physical reality 'augmented with ... computer generated digital images'.

questions.q: What are the four different types of Augmented Reality?
options: Marker-Based, Markerless, Projection Based, Superimposition Based
questions.explanation: L13: 'marker based ..., marker less ..., projection based ..., superimposition based augmented reality'.

questions.q: __ augmented reality is commonly utilized for mapping directions.
questions.explanation: L13: markerless AR uses 'GPS, digital compass or accelerometer ... offering information such as the location'.

questions.q: Which VR type uses head-mounted displays and motion-detecting devices to simulate user’s experiences?
questions.explanation: L13: fully-immersive simulations deliver 'a wide field of view using different head mounted displays, motion detecting devices'.

questions.q: State true or false — “Linear regression, logistic regression, random forest, decision tree are some of the most popular unsupervised learning algorithms”.
questions.explanation: Linear/logistic regression, random forest and decision trees are supervised algorithms, so the statement is false (L14 AI does not list them).

questions.q: A computer program without AI uses __ method whereas computer program with AI uses _ method
options: Large database and algorithmic search, Large knowledge base and heuristic search
Large knowledge base and heuristic search, Large database and algorithmic search
Large knowledge base and algorithmic search, Large database and heuristic search
questions.explanation: L14 AI: 'a computer program without AI uses large databases and ... algorithmic search ... with AI uses large knowledge base and heuristic search'.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct?
options: Machine Learning ⊆ Deep Learning ⊆ Artificial Intelligence
Deep Learning ⊆ Artificial Intelligence ⊆ Machine Learning
Deep Learning ⊆ Machine Learning ⊆ Artificial Intelligence
Artificial Intelligence ⊆ Machine Learning ⊆ Deep Learning
questions.explanation: L14: 'deep learning is a branch of machine learning. Machine learning or deep learning are basically branches of artificial intelligence'.

questions.q: Big data consists of __ .
questions.explanation: L15 Big Data: big data 'exhibit the properties of non-structured data, but they could also have structure data'.

questions.q: What does the word “veracity” indicate in Big Data?
options: It indicates the data which have no restriction over the input data formats.
It indicates velocity of generation of data.
It indicates the data whose meaning is constantly changing.
It indicates biasness in the data, unusualness and noise in data.
questions.explanation: L15: 'Veracity indicates the biasness in the data and ... the unusualness and noise in the data'.

questions.q: Protection of internet-connected systems from cyber-attacks is known as _ .
questions.explanation: L16 Cybersecurity: protection of the internet-connected cyber infrastructure (hardware, software, data) against attacks.

questions.q: In which category of countermeasure does an application firewall fall?
questions.explanation: L16: 'Software level, one could use different application firewalls'.

questions.q: State true or false — “Cybersecurity is recognized as a subset of information security”.
questions.explanation: L16: 'Information security, it is basically recognized as a subset of Cybersecurity'. The statement reverses this.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are correct regarding network security?
options: It provides protection from unofficial access, improper use, fault, deletion, demolition
It is an analytical action which categorizes information benefits.
It ensures the protection of applications from outer threats.
questions.explanation: L16: network security 'would provide protection from unauthorized access, improper use, fault, deletion, demolition'. B is OPSEC and C is application security.

questions.q: What is a malware?
options: A computer program which is used to disturb the computer user, such as computer viruses, spyware etc.
A computer program which breaks security policy to get critical information, which is typically secured.
A computer program which provides a facility to the attacker in which the attacker locks the user’s computer files by using an encryption and demand some money to unlock them.
questions.explanation: L16: 'Malware ... is a computer program which is used to disturb the computer user such as different computer viruses, spyware'.

questions.q: What is SDCMA stand for?
questions.explanation: L16: 'software defined cloud manufacturing architecture' (SDCMA).

questions.q: What are the three key differences between IIoT and Automation?
options: Connectivity, advanced analytics, and IT tools and methodologies
Ubiquitous sensing, advanced analytics, and IT tools and methodologies
Advance sensing, connectivity, and IT tools and methodologies
Ubiquitous sensing, connectivity, and advanced analytics
questions.explanation: L17 Basics of IIoT: differences between IIoT and automation are ubiquitous sensing, analytics, and IT tools and methodologies.

questions.q: What is the role of optimum scheduling in transportation & logistics?
options: It provides good customer services by reducing cancellation and delays.
It provides better safety to both the on boarded passengers and machines.
questions.explanation: L17: 'optimum scheduling we will provide good customer services by reducing cancellations and delays'.

questions.q: Which one of the following digital industrial companies coined the term, Industrial Internet?
questions.explanation: L18 Industrial Internet Systems: 'General Electric, who coined this term industrial internet'.

questions.q: The __ started with the invention of internal combustion engines and electricity
options: First Stage of the Industrial Revolution
Second Stage of the Industrial Revolution
Third Stage of the Industrial Revolution
Fourth Stage of the Industrial Revolution
questions.explanation: L18: 'the second stage ... started in 1870 ... with the invention of the IC engines ... and electricity'.

questions.q: Why is outage a huge problem in power industries?
options: Because the service provided by any power industry is very large.
Because power lines and other equipment are not mobile.
Because replacing a broken equipment is hard.
Because locating a broken power line or equipment is not an easy task.
questions.explanation: L18: 'it is now important to locate the point where the power line is broken or where the equipment ... has gone down'.

questions.q: The emergence of __ system will replace the isolated systems
questions.explanation: L18: 'replacing the isolated systems with the help of cloud-based systems'.

questions.q: Which of the following is a sensors technology manufacturer?
questions.explanation: L19 Industrial Sensing & Actuation: 'DTS, Bosch, Honeywell, OMEGA, these are some of the common sensor manufacturers'.

questions.q: What are the three main modules in PLC architecture?
questions.explanation: L19: 'a typical PLC has three different modules. The CPU module ... power supply module ... input output module'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an actuators technology manufacturer?
questions.explanation: L19 shows an actuator-manufacturers slide without reading names; Moog and Zaber are industrial actuator makers, while Adafruit is a hobby-electronics retailer.

questions.q: Lumada is an IoT platform with advanced AI-based analytics. Which of the following companies created Lumada?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): Hitachi 'have the Lumada IoT platform' providing AI-based advanced analytics.

questions.q: Which type of reference architecture for IIoT enables quick device-to-device integrations, automated data delivery of applications within the buses, isolation of hierarchical subsystems, and integrations of sensors and actuators?
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): layered databus pattern 'allows fast device to device integration with minimum response time, automatic data and application delivery ... hierarchical subsystem isolation'.

questions.q: Values for customer segments in a Business Model can be categorized as _ .
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): value proposition values 'could be quantitative such as price ... or qualitative such as design, customization, customer experience'.

questions.q: Which of the following properties is/are part of the Outcome-based Business Model?
options: Customers are relieved from the responsibilities of ownership and maintenance.
Businesses deliver to the customer the outcome that the product/service provides.
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): outcome-based model - customer 'relieved from the responsibility of ownership and maintenance', pay-per-outcome, and advantages include 'reduced negotiation cycle'.

questions.q: In which of the business models does businesses virtually consolidate and share their IoT-enabled assets among multiple customers or with other business entities in exchange of revenue?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): asset-sharing model is where 'businesses virtually consolidate and share their IoT-enabled assets among multiple customers ... in exchange of revenue'.

questions.q: What is/are the challenges of implementing IoT-as-a-Service?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): IoT-as-a-Service challenges are 'product compatibility, maintaining data accuracy, security of data'; reduced licensing cost and better customer relations are advantages.

questions.q: Platform-as-a-Service is a type of_______________.
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): IaaS, PaaS and SaaS are the three cloud-based service models under the cloud-based IIoT business model.

questions.q: What is/are the challenges(s) of IIoT business model?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): IIoT business model challenges include 'security and data privacy ... lack of interoperability ... increased complexity, increased cost'.

questions.q: Which one of the following is/are core competency(ies) of the Cloud-based IIoT business model?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): cloud-based model core competencies are 'IT resources - software, hardware infrastructure, and the technical knowhow'; platform and data are core competencies of the service/process-oriented models.

questions.q: Which of the following defines IIRA?
options: It is a standard architecture for IIoT systems
It is a business model for IIoT
It is a factory manufacturing IoT products
It is the fourth stage of the Industrial Revolution
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): 'IIRA ... is the architectural standard that is used for most of these IIoT applications'.

questions.q: What is the function of leading KPI?
options: Leading KPI is used to predict the economy
Leading KPI is used to measure the changes in economy after it has begun
Leading KPI is used as a technical indicator of the economy after it has begun
Leading KPI captures the number of fatalities for OSH
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): 'leading KPI ... is mainly used to predict the economy, it is input-oriented, and is hard to measure'.

questions.q: What is Industrial Internet Consortium?
options: A for-profit organization for promotion of open standards
A non-profit organization for promotion of open standards
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): IIC is 'a non-profit consortium ... promoting open standards, standards for interoperability'.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are not part of the IIRA Framework?
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): IIRA framework concepts are stakeholder, viewpoint, architecture frame and architectural representation; no 'position frame'.

questions.q: How many viewpoints are there in the IIRA?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): 'we have the business viewpoint, usage viewpoint, functional viewpoint and the implementation viewpoint' (four).

questions.q: What is Role in context of the Usage viewpoint of IIRA?
options: Describes the functional component of the task maps.
Set of capacities assumed by an entity or organization
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): 'the role is the set of capacities that are assumed by an entity or an organization'.

questions.q: What are the befits of using sensor in industrial applications?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): benefits: real-time monitoring, 'improving the visibility', efficiency ... 'remote diagnostics'.

questions.q: What is the function of LM 35 sensor?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): 'LM 35 is ... an analog temperature sensor, that generates analog voltage'.

questions.q: ADXL335 sensor can generate the magnitude and direction of the acceleration. True or false?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): ADXL335 accelerometer gives X, Y, Z values (magnitude and direction).

questions.q: MQ-2 sensor is used for measuring the concentration of which of the following gases?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): MQ-2 'monitor the concentration of LPG, propane and hydrogen'.

questions.q: __ sensor is used to measure time-varying stresses and strains in ferromagnetic materials?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): 'magnetostrictive sensors ... measure and detect the time varying stresses or strains in ferromagnetic materials'.

questions.q: MOS is one of the electrical variations of gas sensing methods. What is the full form of MOS?
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) gas sensors.

questions.q: What is/are the requirements of industrial communication?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): requirements: real-time, very low duty cycle, very low latency, very low jitter.

questions.q: Industrial Ethernet is used in scenarios that require _ .
options: Local Area Network of field devices
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): fieldbus is for LAN of field devices and 'periodic input-output data transfer', so those are not Industrial Ethernet; Profinet IRT handles clock synchronization (progiez key also (a)).

questions.q: Profinet in industrial communication is based on which of the following technologies?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): 'Profinet is a standard for Industrial Ethernet'.

questions.q: How many active connections or sockets are supported by ModBus-TCP, simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): 'Modbus TCP basically supports up to 10 active connections or sockets at one time'.

questions.q: Which of the following methods is used by EtherCat for bit error recognition?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): EtherCAT uses 'CRC checks ... checksum mechanism' for error detection.

questions.q: What is the full form of Profinet?
questions.explanation: Profinet = PROcess FIeld NETwork (Lecture 29 gives Profibus as process field bus).

questions.q: What is the maximum number of subscribers supported by the Interbus?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): Interbus ring topology 'will provide connectivity to about 512 subscribers'.

questions.q: Select the statement that best describes Tactile Internet.
options: It enables real-time transmission of touch, sense and actuation
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): tactile internet offers 'real time transmission of touch sense ... and actuating' and 'haptic communication'.

questions.q: What is the frequency spectrum for mmWave communication?
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): mmWave communication is in 'the spectrum 30 to 300 Giga hertz band'.

sets.source: https://progiez.com/nptel-introduction-to-industry-4-assignment-7-answers

questions.q: What is the maximum payload of a SIGFOX message?
questions.explanation: 'SIGFOX network gives up to 140 messages per day, with a payload of 12 bytes per message' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: Which of the following modulation techniques is used by LoRA?
questions.explanation: 'LoRa incorporates a spread spectrum modulation technique ... CSS ... Chirp Spread Spectrum' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: Which of the following libraries is used to work with LoRA along with NodeMCU?
questions.explanation: 'You also need this Radiohead library for this LoRa module to work' with NodeMCU (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: Which of the following protocols is used in the physical and MAC layer of the Zigbee communication protocol?
questions.explanation: Zigbee 'follows the specification of IEEE 802.15.4' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: What is a coordinator device in Zigbee network?
options: It is a device to relay information to other nodes in the network
It is a node to generate power for the other nodes in the network
It is only connected to the parent node with no data relaying
It is the root of the network and acts as a bridge between different networks
questions.explanation: 'The coordinator is the root of the network and it acts as the bridge between these different networks' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: XCTU is a software is for configuration of which of the following devices?
questions.explanation: 'XCTU will be used to configure the Xbee modules before they can be used for communication' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: What is/are the characteristic(s) of IIoT data?
options: Correlation in space, time and other dimensions
Temporal and causal relationships in data
questions.explanation: IIoT data characteristics listed: massive polymorphism, real-time, dynamic heterogeneity, temporal/causal relationships, correlation in space, time and other dimensions (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: What is the function of Rule-based engine in Complex Event Processing (CEP)?
options: Extract causal and temporal patterns using predefined rules
Provides services according to device functionality
Handle single data stream at a time
questions.explanation: CEP via rule-based engine: 'it is very important to extract the causal and temporal patterns' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1); other options are middleware/batch distractors.

questions.q: Middleware is a software layer between infrastructure layer and application layer IIoT. True or false?
questions.explanation: 'middleware means it's a software layer which will be standing between the infrastructure layer and the application layer' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: What are the different types of business processing analytics?
questions.explanation: 'business processing analytics could be of three different types ... prescriptive, descriptive or predictive' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: What type of analytics is supported by MIDAS: IoT/M2M platform?
questions.explanation: MIDAS IoT/M2M platform: 'runtime analytics could be performed or batch analytics could be performed' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: Industrial rechargeable sensor network uses __ for grid-based routing and charging. Fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: Not in the lecture transcripts; source paper (Han et al., 'A grid-based joint routing and charging algorithm for industrial wireless rechargeable sensor networks', Computer Networks 2016) proposes proactive (vs passive) charging.

questions.q: What are the 4 major components of an industrial control system?
options: Set points, process variables, controllers, and manipulating variables
Data plane, control plane, variables, and controllers
Set points, dynamic points, variables, and controllers
Feedback loop, controllers, variables, and actuation
questions.explanation: 'four major components': process variable, set points, controller, manipulating variables (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

sets.source: https://progiez.com/nptel-introduction-to-industry-4-assignment-8-answers

questions.q: Which of the following is not a part of IIoT analytics ?
questions.explanation: Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction describes IIoT analytics as real-time/streaming analysis, operations optimization and prognostics (RUL); renewable energy is not an analytics function.

questions.q: Prescriptive analytics is one of the categories of IIoT analytics. True or False?
questions.explanation: Three types: descriptive, predictive, prescriptive (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: Volume, veracity, velocity are the characteristics of which of the following entity?
questions.explanation: Big data: volume, velocity, variability, veracity, variety (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: Feature engineering is absent in which of the following tools or algorithms?
questions.explanation: 'in deep learning ... there is no feature engineering aspects present' (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: What is the purpose of diagnostic analytics ?
options: Detect irregular behavior of assets quickly in the timescale of milliseconds
Identify the root cause of an anomaly in the timescale of minutes
Inform about remaining useful life of an asset
questions.explanation: 'in minutes are diagnostic analytics ... identify the root cause of any anomaly' (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: How many different categories of clustering are there?
questions.explanation: 'two main classifications of clustering algorithms one is known as hard clustering and the other ... soft clustering' (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Fuzzy c-Means Clustering can be used when –
options: Data points may belong to more than one clusters
Data points strictly belong to only one cluster
questions.explanation: FCM: 'one data point may belong to more than one cluster' and 'FCM is extremely faster, much faster compared to the K-means' (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are true about linear regression?
options: It is an unsupervised learning algorithm
It is used to label the data
It is use for prediction of values
questions.explanation: Linear regression is supervised and predicts Y for an unknown X (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Select the machine learning-base IIoT application(s) used in the retail sector?
questions.explanation: 'For retail, product recommendation'; drug discovery = healthcare, dynamic price setup = travel (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Select the correct statement.
options: Artificial intelligence is a subset of machine learning
Machine learning is a subset of deep learning
Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence
Artificial intelligence is a subset of deep learning
